title: Fetch an owner's needed subset by indexed query, write back only changed records

facts.note: Bun conventions catalog; code may run on Node.
Read/write happens in a use case or handler; the fix often lands in the store/adapter.
Hints the task reads a filtered subset of an owner's records.
Static observer must flag `all()`/`list()`/unscoped reads followed by `.filter`/`.sort` in application/route code, awaited store calls inside loops, and save-all/replace-collection writes.
Whether the read set is bounded by records actually used is judged by a reviewer or by a large-history test.

fires: A use case loads every record of an owner (or the whole collection) and filters to the currently valid ones in memory.
A handler sorts an owner's full history in application code to pick the oldest still-open entries.
A use case loops over ids and awaits one store `get` per id.
After changing two records, the code saves the owner's entire record list or the whole collection.
doesNotFire: A store method that already queries by owner with filter/ordering in the adapter, called once per request.
Explicit full-history operations: export, audit report, migration, backfill.
Test fixtures that seed large histories.
Pure domain functions operating on an already-bounded list passed in.

given: A use case or route handler needs a small filtered subset of one owner's records (e.g. currently valid balance entries, open invoices, active bookings) from a store that also keeps that owner's full history.
when: It reads those records and persists the resulting changes.
then: Fetch only the needed subset via a keyed store query (owner + filter + ordering pushed into the store/adapter) and write back only the changed records, so store calls and records touched per request do not grow with the owner's history.
prefer: If missing, add a narrow adapter method, e.g. `findValidByOwner(ownerId: string, at: Date): Promise<Entry[]>` ordered by a key, backed by an index or per-owner structure.
Persist by id: `update(id, patch)` or `updateMany(changed)` for modified records only.
avoid: `(await store.all()).filter(r => r.ownerId === id && r.open).sort(...)` in application code.
Rewriting the whole collection or every owner record after a few changed.
N+1: `for (const id of ids) await store.get(id)`.
Caching or call-count tricks that pass a test while still scanning history.
unless: The operation's output is the full history itself (export, audit report, migration, backfill).
why: Request cost must track the records actually used, not the owner's age; scans of growing history become latency and memory failures for long-lived owners.
evidence: A test seeds a large history (e.g. thousands of inactive/expired records for one owner) and asserts store calls and records read/written per request are bounded by the records actually used, unchanged as the history grows.
Reviewer sees no full-collection or full-owner read in the request path, no in-memory filter/sort of history in the application layer, no store call inside a loop, and writes keyed by id.
verifier_detail: Flag in application/route code: calls to unscoped store reads (`all`, `list`, `findAll`, `getAll`, owner-wide `findByOwner` without filter) followed by `.filter`/`.sort`/`.find` on the result.
Flag awaited store/adapter calls inside `for`/`forEach`/`map` loops over records or ids (N+1).
Flag writes that replace the whole collection or all owner records (`saveAll`, `replaceAll`, writing the full array back) when only a subset changed.
Check that a new query method lives in the store/adapter (integration layer) and is backed by an index, keyed map, or per-owner structure, not by a linear scan inside the adapter.
Large-history test threshold: store calls per request constant (O(1) in history size); records touched <= records used plus a small constant.
Exempt: test files; explicit full-history operations whose output is the history.
audit: Written for PLT-85 as a new general convention; no canonical source YAML. Derived from spec.md.
